samples.summary: The leaf/ancestor directory guard is only tested against fabricated `stat` objects; no test exercises the real filesystem path (symlinked leaf, symlinked ancestor + realpath, unreadable base), so the guard could be inert end to end and every test would still pass.
samples.evidence: `unsafeBaseReason` is unit-tested with hand-built stat literals (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:218-236, 640-676). The only end-to-end CLI guard test is "review refuses a review directory that is not ours" (spec-to-pr.test.mjs ~line 508), which stages a 0755 directory and asserts the mode branch only. Nothing creates a real symlink where the base will be (the documented "classic pre-creation attack": `mkdirSync(requested,{recursive:true})` on a symlink-to-dir succeeds and the writes land elsewhere), nor a symlinked ancestor to prove the `realpathSync` walk both accepts `/var -> /private/var` and still refuses a foreign-owned/world-writable ancestor. If `lstatSync`+`mkdirSync` interact differently than assumed (e.g. mkdirSync throws first, or realpath collapses the leaf), the guard silently stops guarding while the fixture tests keep passing.

samples.summary: `cmdReview`'s own wiring — priorFindingsFor → prepareRoundInputs → panelArgs → the spawned panel — is never executed by a test; only the three pieces in isolation are. A break there silently produces a round that reviews without its carry-forward, which is the exact failure the change exists to prevent.
samples.evidence: `prepareRoundInputs` + `panelArgs` are composed in a test (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:560-586), but that composition is done by the TEST, not by `cmdReview`. No test drives `review` past the dry-run return (the panel is spawned via `execFileSync("node", panelArgs(...))` with no injection seam and no stub), so nothing asserts that `cmdReview` passes `inputs.priorFile`/`inputs.rebuttals` rather than, say, the raw `args.rebuttals` path or `null`. The dry-run branch computes `dryPrior` through a separate code path, so even the dry-run tests do not cover the real argv construction. The file's own docblock names this wiring as the gap three rounds kept raising.

verdict.reason: The symlink/ancestor branches of the base-directory guard have no real-filesystem test anywhere in the repo. `unsafeBaseReason` is exercised only with fabricated stat literals (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:214-237 via the `dirStat` factory, 641-674 via `anc`), including both symlink assertions (lines 226 and 657). A repo-wide sweep for a real link found `symlinkSync` only in scripts/agent/eval/replay-plan.test.mjs:733,756,773,781 and packages/backend/src/lakehouse/lakehouse.service.spec.ts:591 (unrelated modules), and no `ln -s`/`linkSync` in scripts/. Every CLI run of `review` in the suite (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:365,448,517,535,718,766,816) stages plain mkdirSync directories, and no other test file spawns spec-to-pr.mjs. I did find a partial counterexample that narrows the finding: spec-to-pr.test.mjs:507-527 is a real end-to-end test (real 0755 dir, real CLI, real refusal text), so the LEAF guard call at spec-to-pr.mjs:918-919 is provably wired and the reviewer's blanket "could be inert end to end" overstates the leaf case. But the finding still stands where it matters: (1) the ancestor loop at spec-to-pr.mjs:938-945 is witnessed by no test at all — deleting it leaves the suite green, since 507 fails on the leaf and 702-744/746-781 expect success under os.tmpdir(); and (2) nothing distinguishes lstatSync from statSync at line 916, so swapping it would defeat the documented pre-creation symlink attack (spec-to-pr.mjs:515) with every test passing. That is a silently weakened guard over a predictable directory whose contents are read back into a later round's agent prompt, which the rubric grades major.

verdict.reason: No test executes cmdReview's success-path wiring (priorFindingsFor -> prepareRoundInputs -> panelArgs -> spawned panel). cmdReview builds the panel argv at spec-to-pr.mjs:1062-1076 using inputs.priorFile/inputs.rebuttals and spawns path.join(HERE,"review-panel.mjs") (HERE fixed at line 52; no env override or injected spawner anywhere in the file), so there is no seam to stub. Repo-wide greps show panelArgs/prepareRoundInputs/priorFindingsFor exist only in spec-to-pr.mjs and spec-to-pr.test.mjs; no other test file imports the module (review-panel.test.mjs:168 and report-to-pr.test.mjs:219 mention spec-to-pr only in comments). Every CLI test resolves the real script path (361, 434, 508, 530, 703, 752, 811): the dry-run ones return at spec-to-pr.mjs:1018 via the separate dryPrior path, and the two real runs fail earlier — the --rebuttals test (test:535) exits through fail() at spec-to-pr.mjs:1039, the --fresh test (test:766) at the bound refusal (spec-to-pr.mjs:969). The only composition of the pieces (test:562-588) is performed by the test itself, feeding out.priorFile into panelArgs by hand, so nothing would fail if cmdReview passed null or args.rebuttals instead. Real gap over the change's central behavior (silent loss of carry-forward), and in the test-adequacy lane as a missing test for changed behavior.
